name: Hard techno
blurb: A distorted kick with a rumbling tail, and not much else.

sounds.name: Rumble kick
sounds.why: The kick and the bass are the same sound. A copy of the kick is filtered down to a rumble, drowned in reverb, and ducked so it swells up between the hits.

ingredients.name: A plain kick
ingredients.adds: Four kicks to the bar from the default kit.

ingredients.name: Distort it
ingredients.adds: Pushes the kick until it flattens and growls.
ingredients.listenFor: The kick gets longer, louder and angrier.

knobs.above: A burst of noise with no thump.

ingredients.name: Add the rumble
ingredients.adds: A second copy of the kick with only its lowest part left, in a huge reverb.
ingredients.listenFor: A low roar that fills the space between kicks. This is the bassline.

knobs.label: rumble tone
knobs.below: Too low to hear on most speakers.
knobs.above: The rumble turns into audible reverb.

knobs.label: rumble length
knobs.below: The rumble is over before the next kick.

ingredients.name: Duck the rumble
ingredients.adds: Each kick pushes the rumble down for a moment, so it swells back in after.
ingredients.listenFor: Kick, then roar, then kick. They stop overlapping.

knobs.label: duck depth
knobs.below: Kick and rumble are one long blur.
knobs.above: The rumble barely gets back up before the next kick.

pitfalls: Rumble without the duck: the low end is a wall and the kick has no punch.

sounds.why: A loud ride on the offbeat and a clap. At this speed the ride is nearly a continuous wash.

sounds.name: Screech lead
sounds.why: The rave hoover, played higher, shorter and nastier. One or two notes, repeated until the room gives in.

sounds.name: Minor stab
sounds.why: One bare minor chord in a three-against-four rhythm, so it keeps shifting against the kick.

sounds.name: Noise sweep
sounds.why: With no melody to build tension, a rising wall of noise does the job.
The roll before the kick comes back. At 148 BPM the last two bars are a blur.
